Ui.Script:
-- Step the bar one row (the slider's valueStep) — the sensible step for an item list (the -- generic ref scrollbar steps half its height; a discrete row list wants one). Silent by -- design: the ref plays UChatScrollButton only on the arrow *buttons'* OnClick, never on the -- wheel (ScrollFrameTemplate_OnMouseWheel is soundless). Both the wheel and the arrows call -- this, so the click lives on the arrow OnClick, keeping wheel-scroll silent. function BenillaScrollBar_Step(scrollBar, dir) local step = scrollBar:GetValueStep() if step <= 0 then step = 1 end scrollBar:SetValue(scrollBar:GetValue() + dir * step) end
-- Grey the up arrow at the top and the down arrow at the bottom (ref -- ScrollFrame_OnScrollRangeChanged's arrow handling), from the slider's own value/range. function BenillaScrollBar_UpdateArrows(scrollBar) local minV, maxV = scrollBar:GetMinMaxValues() local val = scrollBar:GetValue() local up = getglobal(scrollBar:GetName() .. "ScrollUpButton") local down = getglobal(scrollBar:GetName() .. "ScrollDownButton") if val <= minV then up:Disable() else up:Enable() end if val >= maxV then down:Disable() else down:Enable() end end
-- The scrollbar's OnValueChanged: derive the row offset from the (pixel) value and, only when -- it actually moved, repaint the owner's list. The change-gate is load-bearing: the owner's -- repaint calls _Update below, which SetValue()s the thumb back to offset*itemHeight — a value -- that maps to the SAME offset, so this handler no-ops and the cycle stops after one hop (the -- Slider's own SetValue change-gate stops the value side, decision 0250). -- -- THE SECOND HALF IS FOR ADDONS, and it is the reference's own wiring. The ref's -- `UIPanelScrollBarTemplate` routes its value through the ScrollFrame it rides -- (`<OnValueChanged>this:GetParent():SetVerticalScroll(arg1)</OnValueChanged>`, -- ref-UIPanelTemplates.xml l.156-158), and that frame's `<OnVerticalScroll>` is where an -- addon puts `FauxScrollFrame_OnVerticalScroll(itemHeight, MyUpdate)`. Our OWN faux frames -- are plain `<Frame>`s (the 0251 divergence in the header above), so they have no -- SetVerticalScroll and this line never fires for them — but an addon's is declared -- `<ScrollFrame ... inherits="FauxScrollFrameTemplate">`, and the instance's own tag wins -- over the template's on inherit (framexml.rs `merge`), so it really is one. Duck-typed for -- exactly that reason. -- -- GAP, stated where it bites: `SetVerticalScroll` clamps into `[0, GetVerticalScrollRange()]` -- (scrollframe.rs), and that range comes from the frame's SCROLL CHILD — which the ref's -- `FauxScrollFrameTemplate` declares as `<ScrollChild><Frame name="$parentScrollChildFrame">` -- and our XML loader has no `<ScrollChild>` element for. Until it does, an addon frame's -- range reads 0, so the handler fires with arg1 = 0 and its list stays at the top. The -- offset our own kit computes above is unaffected — it comes straight off the Slider, which -- is the whole point of 0251. function BenillaFauxScrollBar_OnValueChanged(scrollBar, value) local frame = scrollBar:GetParent() local step = scrollBar:GetValueStep() if step <= 0 then step = 1 end local newOffset = floor(value / step + 0.5) if newOffset ~= frame.offset then frame.offset = newOffset if frame.updateFunc then frame.updateFunc() end end BenillaScrollBar_UpdateArrows(scrollBar) if frame.SetVerticalScroll then frame:SetVerticalScroll(value) end end
-- Seat a trough ON ITS BAR. THE SOCKETS, and why this is not a free choice: the channel art -- is not a plain tube — each end carries a 16-tall SOCKET that the arrow button drops into, -- bounded by the frame's outer cap and an inner crossbar. Measured texel-exact off -- UI-Character-ScrollBar (64x256): -- top piece (left column) : rows 0-3 CAP · rows 4-19 SOCKET · rows 20-21 crossbar -- bottom piece (right column): rows 85-86 crossbar · rows 87-102 SOCKET · rows 104-106 CAP -- Both pieces draw 1:1 anchored to their own end of the trough, and the arrow buttons sit 16 -- outside the slider's ends — so a socket lands on its arrow only when the trough OVERHANGS -- the bar by 21 above and 20 below (4 rows of cap at the top against 3+1 at the bottom; that -- 1 is the whole asymmetry). Those are the ref's own numbers, reached from the other side: -- ReputationFrame hangs its trough at the scroll frame's TOPRIGHT (-2,+5) / BOTTOMRIGHT -- (-2,-4) against a bar seated (6,-16)/(6,+16) — 21, 20, and the 8-left hang -- (ref-ReputationFrame.xml l.573-599 against ref-UIPanelTemplates.xml l.166-181). Miss it by -- even 4 and the arrows ride OUT of their sockets onto the caps with a sliver of bare socket -- showing beside them, which is exactly what B224 reported. -- -- Seated HERE, off the bar, rather than restated in each owner's XML: it is one law, and an -- owner made to re-derive it in offsets is an owner that can get it wrong — which is how -- B224 happened. So a trough carries NO anchors of its own; declare it before the bar (so it -- draws beneath) and name it `<barname>Trough`, and that is the whole contract. Lazy, -- because the bar is declared after the trough and does not exist at the trough's OnLoad. function BenillaScrollTrough_Seat(trough, scrollBar) if trough.seated then return end trough.seated = true trough:ClearAllPoints() trough:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", scrollBar, "TOPLEFT", -8, 21) trough:SetPoint("BOTTOMRIGHT", scrollBar, "BOTTOMRIGHT", 7, -20) end
-- Show/hide a bar TOGETHER WITH ITS TROUGH — the recessed channel it rides in, if the -- owner authored one beside it (a `<barname>Trough` frame on BenillaScrollTroughTemplate -- below). Every path that shows or hides a bar goes through here, so a window that fits -- shows neither and one that overflows shows both — and so a trough is seated on its bar -- before it can ever be visible, whichever way the first call goes. -- -- Why the trough is OPT-IN rather than part of the bar template: 1.12 authors trough art -- PER WINDOW, never in the shared scroll kit — `UIPanelScrollBarTemplate` carries only the -- two arrow buttons and the knob, and the ref's FrameXML then hangs loose trough textures -- beside 29 individual bars, in two different skins (UI-Character-ScrollBar for the -- dialog/paperdoll family, UI-ClassTrainer-ScrollBar for the trainer family). The era's own -- MinimalScrollBar went the other way and made its Track part of the bar; this pair keeps -- the era's COUPLING (track lives and dies with the bar) on 1.12's per-window SKIN. function BenillaScrollBar_SetShown(scrollBar, shown) local trough = getglobal(scrollBar:GetName() .. "Trough") if trough then BenillaScrollTrough_Seat(trough, scrollBar) end if shown then scrollBar:Show() if trough then trough:Show() end else scrollBar:Hide() if trough then trough:Hide() end end end
-- **Our trough, following the REFERENCE's bar.** `BenillaScrollBar_SetShown` above is the -- Benilla kit's own pairing and nothing in the reference's faux kit calls it — the -- reference has no trough at all, which is exactly why this template stays ours (1837's -- manifest note). Since the faux frames took the chain's `FauxScrollFrameTemplate` their -- bar is `UIPanelScrollBarTemplate`, so an owner that wants its trough asks for it here, -- right after its `FauxScrollFrame_Update`. Seating is idempotent and the visibility -- simply mirrors the bar's, which the reference's `_Update` has already decided by -- showing or hiding the scroll FRAME. -- -- Decision 1860. Named after the bar rather than the frame because the trough is declared -- `<barname>Trough` — one law, stated once, exactly as BenillaScrollTrough_Seat wants it. function BenillaScrollTrough_Follow(scrollFrameName) local sf = getglobal(scrollFrameName) if not sf then return end local bar = getglobal(scrollFrameName .. "ScrollBar") if not bar then return end local trough = getglobal(bar:GetName() .. "Trough") if not trough then return end BenillaScrollTrough_Seat(trough, bar) if sf:IsShown() then trough:Show() else trough:Hide() end end
-- A wheel spin over the list → one row (WoW convention: +1 up, −1 down). Called from the -- owner window's OnMouseWheel (the engine bubbles the spin up the parent chain, so the handler -- lives on the window, not a child — TrainerFrame.xml's own note). -- -- KEEPS the `Benilla` prefix on purpose: the reference has no faux-scroll wheel function to -- take the name of. Its `ScrollFrameTemplate_OnMouseWheel` is the REAL-scroll one and moves -- by half the bar's height; its faux owners each write a wheel body of their own inline. function BenillaFauxScrollFrame_OnMouseWheel(frame, delta) local scrollBar = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "ScrollBar") BenillaScrollBar_Step(scrollBar, -delta) end
-- ══════════════════════════ The REAL-scroll kit ══════════════════════════════════════════ -- -- The other half of the file: a true `<ScrollFrame>` (engine mechanism, decision 0112) that -- pans and CLIPS a variable-height child, as against the faux kit above (fixed rows re-bound -- to a data offset). Windows whose content height is unknown until it is laid out — a gossip -- menu of wrapped options, a quest's body text — need this one; a uniform list wants the faux. -- -- SHAPE, from the reference `UIPanelScrollFrameTemplate` (Interface\FrameXML\ -- UIPanelTemplates.xml l.166-211, extracted via mpqx): the scrollbar is a SLIDER that rides -- its ScrollFrame as a child, so `bar:GetParent()` IS the frame it scrolls — no name -- derivation, and `$parentBar` gives SyncBar its handle. The ref's OnVerticalScroll drives -- the bar's value and greys the two arrows at the ends; ours does the same through the -- shared arrow helper above. BENILLA_SCROLL_STEP = 20 -- px per arrow click / wheel notch BENILLA_SCROLL_PAD = 20 -- breathing room under the last element in the child
-- The bar moved (drag, arrow, or SyncBar): pan the frame it rides. The loop this could form -- (bar → scroll → OnVerticalScroll → SyncBar → bar) dead-ends in one hop — SyncBar writes the -- value the bar already holds, and the Slider's SetValue change-gate (decision 0250) drops it. function BenillaScrollBar_OnValueChanged(bar, value) bar:GetParent():SetVerticalScroll(value) BenillaScrollBar_UpdateArrows(bar) end
-- Reconcile a ScrollFrame's bar to its live range (ref ScrollFrame_OnScrollRangeChanged): -- the bar spans [0, range] in pixels, seats at the current scroll, and hides entirely when -- the content fits. Wired to both OnScrollRangeChanged and OnVerticalScroll by the owner. function BenillaScroll_SyncBar(sf) local bar = getglobal(sf:GetName() .. "Bar") if not bar then return end local range = sf:GetVerticalScrollRange() bar:SetValueStep(BENILLA_SCROLL_STEP) bar:SetMinMaxValues(0, range) bar:SetValue(sf:GetVerticalScroll()) BenillaScrollBar_UpdateArrows(bar) BenillaScrollBar_SetShown(bar, range > 0) end
-- Pan by `delta` px; the engine clamps to [0, range]. function BenillaScroll_Step(sf, delta) sf:SetVerticalScroll(sf:GetVerticalScroll() + delta) BenillaScroll_SyncBar(sf) end
-- WoW wheel convention: +1 per notch up, -1 down — up lifts the content. function BenillaScroll_OnMouseWheel(sf, delta) BenillaScroll_Step(sf, -delta * BENILLA_SCROLL_STEP) end
-- A widget's resolved bottom edge for the content sum — nil when it isn't contributing -- (hidden frame / blank FontString / not yet resolved this frame). function BenillaScroll_WidgetBottom(w) if not w then return nil end if w.IsShown then if not w:IsShown() then return nil end elseif w.GetText then local t = w:GetText() if not t or t == "" then return nil end end return w:GetBottom() end
-- Size a scroll child to its MEASURED content — the resolved bottom of the lowest visible -- widget, plus padding — instead of a fixed budget, and tell the frame (which fires -- OnScrollRangeChanged → the owner's SyncBar). Frame-late by nature: rects resolve after Lua -- runs, so owners re-run this from an OnUpdate until it stops changing. Returns true when it -- actually resized (only a real change writes: SetHeight invalidates layout, and an -- every-frame write would fight the resolver). function BenillaScroll_ResizeChild(scrollName, widgets) local sf = getglobal(scrollName) -- ASK THE FRAME, don't guess a name. This used to be -- `getglobal(scrollName .. "Child")`, which only ever worked because every caller wore -- a private name in that exact shape — the reference's own convention is -- `<X>ScrollFrame` / `<X>ScrollChildFrame`, not a suffix, so the derivation broke the -- moment QuestFrame took the reference's names. A ScrollFrame knows its own child. local child = sf:GetScrollChild() if not child then return false end local top = child:GetTop() if not top then return false end local bottom = nil for i = 1, table.getn(widgets) do local b = BenillaScroll_WidgetBottom(getglobal(widgets[i])) if b and (not bottom or b < bottom) then bottom = b end end local height = 1 if bottom then height = (top - bottom) + BENILLA_SCROLL_PAD end if height < 1 then height = 1 end if math.abs(child:GetHeight() - height) < 1 then return false end child:SetHeight(height) sf:UpdateScrollChildRect() return true end

-- The placeholder icon for an item/spell whose texture has not arrived yet (Craft, Quest, -- QuestLog, Trainer and TradeSkill read it). Was ActionBar.xml's (stock since 1938), then -- UiPanels.xml's (stock since 1988); this file is the earliest of ours every reader loads -- after. A benilla name, so nothing stock reads it. BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON = "Interface\\Icons\\INV_Misc_QuestionMark"
-- The tab kit — `PanelTemplates_*` — is the REFERENCE's, off the player's chain -- (`Interface\FrameXML\UIPanelTemplates.lua`, seated below this file in the manifest). -- Moved here from our UIParent.lua counterpart with 1988, beside the template that calls it. -- Our eleven transcribed copies stood here dead from the day that entry landed, and one -- of them was carrying a benilla-only return the settle below read (1855/1860). What -- stays is that settle, which is ours because our text measure is a frame late and the -- reference's is not.
-- The tab template's per-frame settle: the ref does TabResize(0) once, in OnShow -- (CharacterFrameTemplates.xml l.77-80), trusting a synchronous text measure. Our -- GetStringWidth has a frame of latency, so the template's OnUpdate calls this until the -- measured width settles (then it's a no-op compare per frame). The ref sizes the hover -- highlight alongside it; this kit does not — both tab templates anchor their highlight to -- their own side edges, so it is the tab by construction and no settle can desync it -- (decision 1004). -- -- The fit PARAMETERS live on the tab (`benillaTabPadding`/`benillaTabMaxWidth`, defaulting -- to the +0 fit every window tab has always used) rather than at the call site, because -- there is exactly one call site and it is this settle loop: an instance that ran its own -- TabResize in OnLoad — as the reference's macro tabs do — would just be overwritten on the -- next frame. Setting the two fields IS how an instance asks for the reference's own fit. -- THE STRUCTURAL CLAMP — a tab may never grow past its window's drawn right edge, whatever -- the instance asked for (decision 1002; the director's "fix this properly to prevent it -- ever again"). The reference's own caps are numbers hand-tuned to ITS font: the macro -- window's 150 is right for the enUS FRIZQT__ the 1.12 client rasterizes and for nothing -- else in particular, and the label it guards carries a CHARACTER NAME — the one string -- whose width no window author can know. So the instance's cap is a preference and the -- window's edge is the law. -- -- `benillaTabRightInset` is how a window declares how far its DRAWN plate stops short of -- its frame rect, because no kit can introspect an art margin. The macro window's is 40: -- its 384-unit frame is painted by a 256-wide slice plus a 128-wide one that carries a -- transparent tail. Clamping to the frame rect instead — the first attempt — clamped to a -- boundary the player cannot see, and the tab still walked out over the world. -- -- The clamp is applied to the RESULT, through TabResize's own `absoluteSize` arm, rather -- than folded into `maxWidth`: that parameter is compared against `text + padding` but -- assigned as `maxWidth + padding`, so a room budget expressed through it is off by the -- padding and silently fails to bind. `absoluteSize` sets the tab width outright, which is -- exactly what a room budget is. function BenillaTab_Room(tab) local parent = tab:GetParent() if not parent then return nil end local left, right = tab:GetLeft(), parent:GetRight() if not left or not right then return nil end local room = (right - (tab.benillaTabRightInset or 0)) - left if room < 1 then room = 1 end return room end
function BenillaTabButton_OnUpdate(tab) local name = tab:GetName() local text = getglobal(name .. "Text") local w = (text and text:GetStringWidth()) or 0 if w <= 0 then return end local pad = tab.benillaTabPadding or 0 local room = BenillaTab_Room(tab) if tab.benillaFitWidth == w and tab.benillaFitRoom == room then return end tab.benillaFitWidth, tab.benillaFitRoom = w, room PanelTemplates_TabResize(pad, tab, nil, tab.benillaTabMaxWidth) -- THE CLAMP READS THE FIT BACK OFF THE ART, not off a return value and not off the -- button. `PanelTemplates_TabResize` is the REFERENCE's now (1837 put -- `UIPanelTemplates.lua` on the chain below this file, so its definition wins) and it -- returns nothing; our own copy's benilla-only `return tabWidth` had already stopped -- running, which is what took 1002's clamp off the air silently. `tab:GetWidth()` -- cannot serve either — it reads the last RESOLVED rect, this frame's stale input -- inside a settle, which is the whole reason 1002 added that return. -- -- `$parentMiddle` can. `PanelTemplates_TabResize` sets it on its way out, a Texture's -- width is its AUTHORED size, and a region's GetWidth reports the authored value -- without consulting a resolved rect (region::virtual_span) — so it is the number the -- verb just computed, same tick. The tab is that plus its two end caps, which is the -- reference's own `tabWidth = width + sideWidths`. if room then local middle = getglobal(name .. "Middle") local left = getglobal(name .. "Left") local fitted = (middle and middle:GetWidth() or 0) + 2 * (left and left:GetWidth() or 0) if fitted > room then PanelTemplates_TabResize(pad, tab, room) end end -- No highlight sizing here on purpose — BOTH tab templates anchor their highlight to -- their own two side edges, so it IS the tab by construction (decision 1004). end
